newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Philippines and other Southeast Asian neighbours have begun massive operations to withdraw citizens from war-torn Cambodia, as international pressure mounted on Second Prime Minister Hun Sen. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Ramos yesterday said the government would not relent in defending the peso against speculative attacks amid what he called deliberate efforts from outside forces to undermine the peso and the disinformnation campaign in the media. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Moro Islamic Liberation Front yesterday said it welcomed but will not reciprocate the government's declaration of suspension of military operations in Mindanao. (JOURNAL/STANDARD)
- Persistent rumours on a possible devaluation of the peso continued to hound the local currency market yesterday. The Monetary Board ruled out a devlaution of the peso. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Car sales in the first half of this year dropped by 7.8 percent to 40,478 units from 43,879 in the same period last year due to a technical correction after strong sales last year, the Chamber of Automotive Manufacturers of the Philippines Inc said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The government expected to attain an 8.9 billion-peso fiscal surplus for the whole year of 1997 in compliance with the "best effort" revenues it pledged with the International Monetary Fund, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said. (CHRONICLE/BULLETIN)
